name: Fix It for Everyone

pick.label: Pick something annoying
pick.heading: Pick something annoying and fix it for everyone
lead: Lots of everyday things are hard to use, and not only for some people. Try opening a jar with wet hands, using a ticket machine in bright sunshine, or reading tiny instructions without your glasses.

Choose something that annoys you and redesign it so that more people can use it. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *If it’s easier for one person, it’s often easier for lots of people.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: I am not looking for a finished product here, this is just for a bit of fun. Some fixes are genuinely clever, and some only make sense at two in the morning. Both are welcome.

rows: Which annoying thing are you redesigning?
What exactly makes it hard to use? Be specific.
Who has the most trouble? Think of people in a hurry, carrying shopping, wearing gloves, in bright sunlight…
What do you change? The shape, the size, the colour, the words, the whole idea?
Give your new version a name.
Who else does your fix help, apart from the people you started with?

values.problem: The lid is small and smooth, and it was screwed on by a machine much stronger than me. I lose this fight every Sunday morning.
values.who: People with weak or sore hands, anyone whose hands are wet or covered in butter, and me.
values.fix: A lid with a little fold-out lever, like a tiny handle, so you turn it with your whole hand and not just your fingertips.
values.name: The Lid Lad
values.everyone: Kids can make their own breakfast, nobody has to bang the jar on the table, and I keep a little bit of dignity.

yours.label: Your fix
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your fix in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which fix wins?
rank.placeholder: The fix, e.g. The Lid Lad
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their fix in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
